title: Collective Strong Quantum Mpemba Effect in Accelerated Quantum Detectors
authors: G. D. de Moraes Neto, Richard Q. Matos, Norton G. de Almeida
abstract: Collective coupling to the Minkowski vacuum allows uniformly accelerated quantum detectors to exhibit a strong quantum Mpemba effect, in which a state initially farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than a closer one. We establish the existence of this effect for every fixed finite number of detectors $N\geq 2$ at sufficiently small transverse separation within the pointlike secular master equation. The mechanism originates from two reflection sectors whose populations are conserved by the leading collective dynamics. Weak intersector transfer at finite separation generates an isolated, parametrically slow relaxation mode. A simple family of initial states permits its leading-order cancellation by matching the equilibrium sector populations, while a corrected preparation eliminates the slow-mode amplitude exactly. We construct a reference state that establishes a genuine reversal of trace-distance ordering. Numerical calculations and local-rate-preserving controls identify the collective origin of the effect, while spatially smeared detector calculations support its persistence within the second-order secular framework. The same mechanism extends to detectors coupled to a common thermal field, with analytically distinct slow relaxation rates. Thus, strong Mpemba relaxation is not exclusive to acceleration but emerges from a more general interplay between collective dissipation, reflection-sector conservation, and weak symmetry-breaking transfer.
summary: This theoretical paper proves the existence of a strong quantum Mpemba effect in an array of accelerated quantum detectors. The effect arises from collective dissipation mechanisms involving the conservation of specific reflection sectors. It demonstrates that the relaxation ordering can be reversed by carefully preparing the initial quantum state.
main_problem: The paper investigates the 'strong quantum Mpemba effect,' where a quantum state initially farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than a state initially closer to equilibrium.
main_result: The effect is rigorously established for multiple detectors coupled to a vacuum or thermal field, stemming from the interplay between collective dissipation and conserved reflection sectors.
method: The analysis uses the point-like secular master equation, spectral analysis, and projection techniques to track the slow relaxation mode.
model_or_system: The system consists of N identical two-level Unruh-DeWitt detectors collectively coupled to a common massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum or a common thermal field.
key_observables: Trace distance decay, slow relaxation rates ($ ar{\gamma}_{	ext{slow}}$), and the spectral enhancement factor ($R$).
important_parameters: Number of detectors ($N \ge 2$), transverse separation ($d$), and the acceleration parameter ($E$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the point-like secular master equation and relies on the existence of two conserved reflection sectors.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry of the detector array, comparing trace distance decay curves for optimized vs. reference states, and showing the dependence of the optimal preparation parameter and spectral enhancement factor on system parameters.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by analyzing the master equation, identifying the slow relaxation mode generated by weak intersector transfer, constructing specific initial states to demonstrate the reversal of relaxation ordering, and generalizing the mechanism to thermal fields.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, non-trivial example of non-equilibrium dynamics in an open quantum system, directly addressing the Mpemba effect in a quantum context relevant to quantum field theory and quantum optics.
